newsitem.title: GERMANY: INSTANT VIEW - EU Commission forecast for Germany.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - EU Commission forecast for Germany.

text.p: Following are economists' reactions to the EU Commission's forecast that the German budget deficit will amount to 3.0 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) in 1997, exactly matching the reference level set for nations wishing to qualify for European monetary union.

UWE ANGENENDT, BHF-BANK - "I think these figures are problematic. Our forecast for the German budget deficit-to-GDP rate in 1997 is 3.3 percent and that is based on the assumption that the May official tax revenue estimate will be eight to 12 billion marks below the previous estimate. If the revenue shortfall is bigger more budget measures will be needed to keep the deficit at this level and that will be difficult to achieve even with a spending freeze. But if the tax shortfall is 20 billion marks as predicted by the six research institutes then I don't know how it will be possible to come close to the three percent criterion."

HOLGER FAHRINKRUG, UBS FRANKFURT: "My forecast for the German deficit-to-GDP rate is 3.4 percent. It is conspicuous that the Commission's forecasts for a lot of EU countries are exactly at 3.0 percent. The Commission's forecast for Germany is the most optimistic of all possibilities. It is theoretically possible but not without a tax increase and/or further substantial savings efforts. A deficit at 3.4 percent would not prevent Germany from qualifying for monetary union. It would be hard to imagine monetary union being delayed for that reason. Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer is sensible in saying that it is more important to look at the sustainability of the criteria."

HANS-JUERGEN MELTZER, DB RESEARCH: "Of course the forecast is optimistic but the six institutes said a deficit of 3.0 percent was possible. It's still on the optimistic side and it depends on further savings measures by the government. It seems optimistic now but could be realistic in two months. Our forecast for the deficit is 3.3 percent without savings measures and 3.0 percent if the government saves an additional 10 billion marks."
